required_facts_checked: DataTalks.Club cohorts bring repeated questions into Slack, including joining, Windows setup, homework submission and broken steps.
The FAQ grew to about 1,300 entries across Zoomcamps, with roughly 500 in the Data Engineering Zoomcamp FAQ.
Community member Alex Litvinov built the RAG-powered Slack bot.
The bot ingests FAQ entries, Slack history, GitHub repositories and YouTube subtitles, with structure-preserving chunks.
The bot uses a daily Prefect pipeline in Docker, LlamaIndex, BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 embeddings, Zilliz Cloud, Cohere Rerank and GPT-4o-mini among its components.
The bot keeps separate course query engines, routes by Slack channel ID, retrieves 20 candidates, applies time weighting and reranks to four.
The FAQ migrated from Google Docs to Git and a static website after moderation and parsing problems.
The migration downloads DOCX, extracts content with Python's docx module, cleans formatting with GPT-4o and stores course/module/question Markdown files with frontmatter.
Jekyll conflicted with dbt's Jinja syntax, so a custom Python generator with GitHub Copilot help produced HTML and JSON exports.
The generator exports courses.json and per-course JSON for programmatic indexing with minsearch.
Fred Pearce built the GitHub Actions workflow around the FAQ Automation Bot.
The bot returns NEW, UPDATE or DUPLICATE decisions and human review with Claude Code remains in the loop.
unsupported_claims_removed: Removed claims that the bot or generator was error-free, fully autonomous or reusable outside this project.
Removed unsupported causal explanations beyond the documented vandalism, parsing and contribution-friction problems.
substantive_edits: Rewrote the workflow as a source-first explanation from repeated Slack questions through retrieval, migration, generation and issue automation.
Attributed Alex Litvinov's bot and Fred Pearce's GitHub Actions work explicitly.
Preserved the human Claude Code review step and the structured NEW, UPDATE and DUPLICATE decision model.
